name: Mount Feathertop
bio_draft: Mountain, the second highest peak in Victoria, reached by the Feathertop Track from Harrietville.

facts.claim: Mount Feathertop is the second-highest mountain in Victoria, at 1,922 metres, in the Alpine National Park.
Snow lingering in the summit gullies until late spring gives the feathered look behind the name.
The North Razorback track is the shortest and easiest route; the South Razorback from Diamantina Hut is 11 km to the summit.
Routes are exposed in bad weather, and there are two refuge huts.

access_note: Exposed ridge, weather-dependent; Parks Victoria lists reported issues for the park

name: Falls to Hotham Alpine Crossing
bio_draft: Multi-day alpine walk between Falls Creek and Mount Hotham, one of the high country's long walks.

facts.claim: A 37 km three-day hike through the Alpine National Park from Falls Creek to Mt Hotham.
Day 1 passes Heathy Spur lookouts and historic Wallace and Cope huts; day 2 has panoramas from Pole 333 and views of Mount Feathertop.
Day 3 passes the abandoned Quintet Mine and Derricks Hut before finishing at Mt Hotham.
Overnight camping needs a permit booked through Parks Victoria; open for hiking roughly November to April (sources).

access_note: Walk is free; camping permit/fee is extra and not the price. Parks Victoria page carries a track-closure notice (storm/flood damage). Snow-bound roughly June-October.
unresolved: Camping permit fee not captured; the walk itself is free (Victorian national park)

name: The Razorback
bio_draft: Ridge walk above Mount Hotham with views over the Alps.

facts.claim: The Razorback is the exposed ridge linking Mount Hotham to Mount Feathertop; the South Razorback starts at Diamantina Hut on the Great Alpine Road near Mt Hotham.
It is 11 km from the Diamantina Hut start to the Mount Feathertop summit and relatively flat.
It is a popular summer walk and a winter ski tour, but very exposed in bad weather.

name: Mount Buller
bio_draft: Ski resort and alpine village on Mount Buller, with summer walking and mountain biking.

facts.claim: Mount Buller Alpine Resort has a ski area from 1,375 m to 1,780 m with 85 trails and about 40,000 skiers/hr lift capacity.
In summer a Sightseeing Chairlift gives High Country views, and the resort offers hiking, mountain biking and RockWire, Australia's first via ferrata.
The village is about 3 hours from Melbourne.
The resort is an unincorporated area surrounded by the Shire of Mansfield.

access_note: Winter gate entry fee ($69 per vehicle, single day, 9 seats or fewer) applies only in the snow season, not summer; per vehicle so not used as the price. Lift tickets/activities extra.

name: Mount Stirling
bio_draft: Alpine resort and summit with summit loop walks and cross-country tracks.

facts.claim: Mt Stirling Alpine Resort is a patrolled cross-country and backcountry ski area with about 60 km of cross-country trails (secondary).
The Stirling summit (about 1,749 m) has a summit loop walk and year-round camping.
Access is via Mansfield and the Mt Buller Tourist Road past the Mirimbah gate.
Other activities include snowshoeing, tobogganing and snow play in winter.

access_note: Winter gate fee $69 per vehicle (covers Buller and Stirling), snow season only, not summer; per-night camping fee applies year-round from 1 June 2026.

name: Lake Eildon
bio_draft: Large reservoir on the Goulburn River with houseboats, fishing and boating.

facts.claim: Lake Eildon is a large reservoir impounded by Eildon Dam on the Goulburn River, with a capacity of 3,390 GL.
The surrounding Lake Eildon National Park offers swimming, canoeing, waterskiing, sailing and fishing.
Merlo Lookout and the Blowhard Summit walk give views over the lake, and houseboats can be hired from local companies.
Herb Fitzroy and Forsyth Flat have free gas barbecues and boat ramps.

access_note: Park page shows reported issues/closure notices; check before visiting. Houseboat hire and camping are extra.

name: Craig's Hut Walk
bio_draft: Walk to a historic hut near Mount Stirling.

facts.claim: Craig's Hut was built in 1982 as the set for the film The Man from Snowy River.
It stands on Mount Stirling and is reached on foot from the Circuit Road Picnic Area (about 1.2-1.7 km one way, around 3 km return).
Vehicle access to the area is subject to a seasonal winter closure.

access_note: Seasonal winter road closure to the picnic area; sources disagree on distances.

name: Mount Howitt Walking Track
bio_draft: Walking track on Mount Howitt, a high country summit walk.

facts.claim: The standard route is about 14 km return (around 5 hours) from the Howitt car park to the 1,742 m summit cairn.
It climbs through snow gum forest to Macalister Springs, where the Vallejo Gantner Hut stands, then meets the Australian Alps Walking Track.
Lies in Alpine National Park; the access road is usually open November to May and the last 58 km from Melbourne side is unsealed.

name: Lake Eildon National Park
bio_draft: National park around Lake Eildon with boating, fishing and walks.

facts.claim: A national park around Lake Eildon with swimming, canoeing, waterskiing, sailing and fishing in the shadow of the Victorian Alps.
Merlo Lookout and the Blowhard Summit walk give views over the lake towards Mount Buller.
Herb Fitzroy and Forsyth Flat have free gas barbecues and boat ramps; Candlebark Campground is a base for walking and paddling.

name: Mount Samaria State Park
bio_draft: State park with bushwalks and lookouts on Mount Samaria near Strath Creek.

facts.claim: A semi-remote state park on a plateau formed by volcanic activity in the Devonian, jointly managed with Taungurung Traditional Owners.
Tracks from the central gravel road lead to 360-degree views from the summit of Mount Samaria and to Wild Dog Falls and Back Creek Falls.
Remnant kilns and sawdust mounds from 1920s logging remain; the tall forest shelters the Greater Glider and spring brings wildflowers.
Free camping facilities are available in the park.

name: Lake Nillahcootie
bio_draft: Reservoir near Barjarg with fishing, boating and lakeside picnic areas.

facts.claim: Nillahcootie Dam, completed in 1967, holds a 40,400 ML reservoir in the Victorian Alps.
It is a popular water-skiing lake in summer.
A boat ramp at the northern end has a large car park, toilets and a mobile coffee van most days.

name: Mansfield Zoo
bio_draft: Zoo on the Mansfield-Woods Point Road with native and exotic animals.

facts.claim: Zoo on 30 acres of parkland with views across the Delatite Valley to Mount Buller.
Visitors hand or spade feed deer, kangaroos, wallabies, emu, ostrich and llamas; the zoo also keeps white lions, capuchin monkeys, a camel and meerkats.
Lion and meerkat feeding is at 1.30pm on weekends and Victorian public and school holidays; overnight camping is offered.

name: Harrietville
bio_draft: Village above the snowline at the foot of Mount Feathertop, a base for alpine walks.

facts.claim: Village at about 510 m elevation at the head of the Ovens Valley, postcode 3741
Walking tracks around the village include the Tronoh Dredge hole circuit and the East Ovens River Track

facts.claim: Small village about 6 km south of Bright

name: Tronoh Dredge Walking Track
bio_draft: Walking track past a gold dredge at Harrietville.

facts.claim: Roughly 1.4-1.5 km loop around the dredge hole, a man-made lake, about 30 min
Tronoh Dredge was one of the world's largest electric-powered dredges, operating 1942 to 1954
Starts at Tronoh Dredge car park off Feathertop Track; reserve is run by volunteer committees, not Parks Victoria

name: Mount Beauty Gorge Walk
bio_draft: Short walk through the gorge near Mount Beauty.

facts.claim: Track from Big Hill Mountain Bike Park via the Aqueduct Track about 1 km to a swing bridge over the West Kiewa River
Beyond the bridge is a swimming hole and the 1950s adit dug for the Kiewa hydro scheme
In dry summer you can wade and swim 400 m upstream to a canyon; river levels can rise suddenly because it is part of the hydro scheme

access_note: Water flows may rise without warning (hydro scheme)

name: Old Beechworth Gaol
bio_draft: Restored 1850s gaol in Beechworth, open for tours of cells and the Ned Kelly connection.

facts.claim: Completed in 1864; held Ned Kelly, his brother Dan, and Ellen Kelly; closed in 2004
Built of granite quarried on site; part of the Beechworth Historic Precinct on the National Heritage List
Guided tours about 45 minutes, run daily

bio_draft: Historic gold town with a main street of heritage buildings and walks around it.

facts.claim: Historic centre classified by the National Trust, with many original shopfronts
Self-guided 'A Walk in High Street' covers 37 historic sites
Nearby gold-era Karr's Reef mine tours and a gorge walk along an old sluicing race

name: Chiltern
bio_draft: Historic gold town with a well-preserved streetscape used as a film set.

facts.claim: Gold-rush town about 25 km from Beechworth with a preserved 19th-century main street.
Dow's Pharmacy, a National Trust property, operated as a chemist from 1859 to 1968 and was donated intact in 1988.
Lake View House, a National Trust property overlooking Lake Anderson, was the childhood home of author Henry Handel Richardson.

access_note: Dow's Pharmacy charges adults $10 (combined ticket with Lake View House $15) but that is an extra inside the town, not the price of the spot.

name: Lake Sambell
bio_draft: Lake and parkland in Beechworth with a walking track around it.

facts.claim: Lake and parkland in Beechworth with a roughly 2 km circuit and a bird hide.
The Lake Sambell to Lake Kerferd walk runs through eucalypt forest of Beechworth Historic Park with traces of old mining.
Walking is free; dogs are permitted on leash in the historic park.

name: Chiltern-Mount Pilot National Park
bio_draft: National park of box-ironbark forest with walking tracks around Chiltern.

facts.claim: Park of about 21,636 ha of open eucalypt forest (red stringybark, mugga ironbark) between Beechworth and Chiltern.
Mount Pilot Lookout is a short walk from the car park to the 545 m summit, with 360-degree views toward Mount Buffalo.
The Whitebox Walking Track is an 8.5 km, 2-3 hour walk from Honeyeater Picnic Area; Woolshed Falls is a 10 minute drive north of Beechworth.

name: Eldorado Dredge
bio_draft: Restored gold dredge at Eldorado, with a walking track and a picnic area.

facts.claim: Large steel gold dredge built 1935-36 by Thompson's Engineering for the Cocks Eldorado Gold Dredging Company.
It has 110 digging buckets and dredged 30 million cubic metres from the Eldorado Plain before being decommissioned.
It is on the Eldorado-Byawatha Road on the edge of Eldorado and holds an Engineers Australia heritage marker.

name: Yackandandah Gorge Scenic Walk
bio_draft: Scenic walk beside the gorge at Yackandandah.

facts.claim: Walk along a historic gorge dug as a tail race to sluice gravel and sand in the gold rush.
The trail follows a creek with cascading waterfalls and shady trees; the top of the gorge is steep.
A car park with information signs marks the start; walking from town along the creek takes about an hour.

name: Glenrowan
bio_draft: Small town where Ned Kelly was captured in 1880, with Kelly sites and a statue.

facts.claim: Small town where Ned Kelly and his gang made their last stand in June 1880.
Ned Kelly's Last Stand animated theatre at the Glenrowan Tourist Centre re-enacts the siege; Kate's Cottage and Kelly Museum, plus the Big Ned statue, are in town.
The Ned Kelly Discovery Hub at Lions Park tells the 1880 siege story and includes the original railway station.

access_note: Paid attractions inside town are extras; price not recorded.
